result.topic_en: Euler restricts attention to the case where the formula V contains only first-order differentials, states the two governing equations N dx = dP and N' dx = dP', and derives an auxiliary third equation by substituting into dV, introducing S = V - Pp - P'p'.
result.transcription:
23
haecque solutio adeo patet, ad quotcunque gradus differentialia, in formula V contenta, ascendant.
10. Cum autem solutiones talium problematum altiora differentialia implicantium, plerumque nimis evadant difficiles atque adeo plerumque plane intractabiles, hic tantum casus simpliciores, quibus differentialia in formula V non ultra primum gradum ascendant, attentius sumus contemplaturi, quae ergo ex his duabus aequationibus erunt petendae:
I. $N\partial x = \partial P$ et II. $N'\partial x = \partial P'$.
11. Quamquam autem hae duae aequationes totum negotium conficere sunt censendae; tamen plerumque plurimum expediet iis adhuc tertiam quandam aequationem, quae quidem in iis jam contineatur, adjungere, quippe quae calculo sublevando plurimum inserviet. Quoniam enim posuimus $\partial y = p\partial x$ et $\partial z = p'\partial x$, ex illis duabus aequationibus elicimus:
1°. $N\partial y = p\partial P$ et 2°. $N'\partial z = p'\partial P'$,
qui valores, in formula differentiali generali:
$\partial V = M\partial x + N\partial y + N'\partial z + P\partial p + P'\partial p'$,
substituti, producent hanc formam:
$\partial V = M\partial x + p\partial P + P\partial p + p'\partial P' + P'\partial p'$, sive
$\partial V = M\partial x + \partial .(pP + p'P')$.
Hinc ergo, si brevitatis gratia ponamus $V - Pp - P'p' = S$,

items.quote: hic tantum casus simpliciores, quibus differentialia in formula V non ultra primum gradum ascendant, attentius sumus contemplaturi
items.english: here we shall consider more attentively only the simpler cases, in which the differentials in the formula V do not rise beyond the first degree

items.quote: Quamquam autem hae duae aequationes totum negotium conficere sunt censendae; tamen plerumque plurimum expediet iis adhuc tertiam quandam aequationem, quae quidem in iis jam contineatur, adjungere, quippe quae calculo sublevando plurimum inserviet.
items.english: Although these two equations must be considered to settle the whole matter, it will usually be very useful to add to them a certain third equation, which is indeed already contained in them, since it will greatly serve to ease the calculation.
